Strong Kenya presence with Nairobi office and established relationships with WFP, UNHCR, and UN agencies
Bilingual team capability (English and Somali/Swahili) essential for Dadaab refugee camp operations
Proven track record with refugee and displacement programming in Somalia and Kenya
Experience with community engagement, protection, and participatory approaches aligned with GFD requirements
Established compliance frameworks (PSEA policy, child safeguarding, ISO certification) meeting WFP standards
Past experience with multiple UN agencies and humanitarian partners suitable for coordinating with WFP, UNHCR, DRS, and refugee leadership
key_gaps:
No explicit evidence of large-scale food distribution or commodity management experience (GFD is operational logistics-heavy, not primarily research/MEL-focused)
Cortech's core strength is in monitoring, evaluation, research, and capacity building — not operational programme implementation at scale
Limited evidence of experience implementing Differentiated Assistance frameworks or Cash-Based Transfer (CBT) systems
No mention of biometric verification system expertise (WFP-specific technical requirement)
Cortech's typical budget range ($1,000–$300,000) may be significantly lower than the full-year operational cost of running two refugee camps' GFD
This is a Cooperating Partner (implementation) role, not an assessment/evaluation role where Cortech excels
